description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The soak's check quotes the lines a game's log writes as its main loop is asked to end, so a game that ends of its own says what asked.
At Low a surface by a wall thinner than the field's cell reads the world's probes through the field, so a lamp outside a room of thin walls lights none of its floor inside.
The screen's probes stand further apart past 1080 pixels high, every 16 at High at 3840 by 2160, and the guide gives their cost at four sizes of window.
The screen's probes come with Medium and High and Low leaves them out for the glow lights' probes alone, the call that left them out gone and a debugging toggle leaving them out whole at any quality.
The counted corners shader names its vertex index with a word Metal leaves free, and a test holds every built-in shader's names clear of the words Metal keeps.
A mesh over shader buffers takes each vertex's color beside a stream of the program's own, and lies in a range of larger buffers with a count of its own.
Tempo's autopilot plays each note its frame's step of the song passed at the note's own time on the song's clock, so a stalled frame misses none.
The far cascade holds a thin sheet as thin as the last counted cascade does and is read only by rays leaving the counted cascades, so its slab is gone.
The behaviors guide shows a voxel world's section as a mesh entity, with a thousand meshes read against DrawMesh.
A sound's voice is fed through a low-pass at its cutoff and the room's reverb at its share, the room set by size and decay.
A voice played once flushes its resampled streams, so a sound whose rate differs from the device's ends under the dummy driver and on a real device alike.
A voice played once is let go as it plays out, so each tick walks the voices still playing and the profile counts them.
The world keeps an index of the many entities under each key a component names, walked as a span.
A program's profile value can be shown as the mean of the values set over a window of seconds.
A particle emitter's squares face the camera, a normal it gives or the way each particle moves.
A particle emitter steps, sorts and draws only the slots that may hold a live particle, so an empty one costs nothing.
A mesh entity draws through its material's shader, hides by a Visible bool, casts shadow alone by a ShadowOnly one and counts its draws in the profile.
A behavior reads how far the mouse wheel turned in the frame through its context's input.
A behavior's method orders its system after or before another by attributes and runs only while each of several states holds.
The engine's curve bends each channel past a knee of 0.8 toward white on its own unless SetHighlightKnee says otherwise, so the bounce rooms' strip lamp shows white as its reference does, seven reference frames written again in their highlights alone, saved with the strip and the window against their references with the knee off and on.
title: 3DEngine
